_design: PRE-REGISTERED before any agent ran. 12 authoring briefs in AUTHOR voice — the words a person writing a deck would use, deliberately NOT the manifests' vocabulary, because a brief phrased in manifest prose hands the full-catalog condition a verbatim string match and measures nothing. Ground truth is a SET: `expect` is the component the manifest's own whenToUse points at, `ok` are alternatives a competent author could defend. Scored on `expect` (strict) and `expect ∪ ok` (lenient). Bias risk, stated: the same person wrote these and both surfaces, so a brief could unconsciously favor vocabulary the pick row happens to carry. Mitigation is only partial — briefs were written from whenToUse SITUATIONS, then the ground truth locked, before either agent was spawned.

briefs.brief: Closing slide of a board update. I want the quarter's revenue number to hit hard and nothing else on the slide to compete with it.
Four metrics for the monthly ops review — each needs a label, the value, and whether it's on track or slipping.
Onboarding deck. Six things a new hire does in their first week, in order, each needing a sentence of explanation.
We evaluated five vendors against seven criteria — price, support, SLA, integrations, and so on. The audience wants to scan the whole grid.
Plot our twelve product lines by growth rate against margin so the room can see which quadrant each falls in.
The delivery plan: three workstreams across four quarters, with some tasks overlapping and a couple of milestones.
This deck is full of internal acronyms. I want one slide defining about ten of them, term on the left, meaning on the right.
End of an investor pitch — the four questions we always get asked, each with our answer.
Credibility slide: show the eight customer brands that use us. The names are the whole argument.
Engineering deep-dive. I need to show a fifteen-line function and walk through why it's written that way.
Compliance deck. One statute passage needs to sit on its own slide with the citation, because everything after it depends on that exact wording.
A slide that just marks the transition into the second half of the deck. No content, just a clean break.

_correction: Ground truth initially listed `statement` three times — that is a BUCKET, not a component. Caught by validating every name against loadAll() BEFORE running, the same check the pick surface now applies to its see-also column. Replaced with real members (premise/quote/kpi/title).
